chunks: Sa'd, from Abū Ja'far, from his father, from 'Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū 'Abd Allāh, from his father, from 'Alī عليه السلام.
That he would not raise his hands in the جنازة except once, meaning in the takbīr.

So the proper understanding regarding these two narrations is a mode of permissibility and the lifting of obligation, even though what is more excellent is what the earlier narrations contained. And it is possible that they were issued in the context of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of many among the العامة.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation practiced for protection in certain circumstances
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: the utterance of takbīr in the prayer
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلُ: the more virtuous or preferable practice
key_terms.الْجِنَازَةِ: the funeral prayer context being discussed
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْوُجُوبِ: removal of obligation from an act

ai.seo_question: Is raising the hands in every takbīr of the funeral prayer obligatory or merely permissible?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling on raising the hands during the takbīrs of the funeral prayer. It indicates that not raising them except once is permissible and not obligatory, while affirming that the preferable practice is what the earlier narrations mentioned, with the possibility that this report was given under taqiyyah.
